name: Optimazz – Website Optimization and Speedup
author: Shipon Karmakar

sections.description:
Optimazz is an all-in-one performance suite that applies the optimizations with the biggest impact on Core Web Vitals — automatically and safely. Every module is opt-in and reversible, and Optimazz never overwrites another caching plugin’s files.

Modules included:

  • Page Cache — serve static HTML instead of running PHP on every request, with smart exclusions (logged-in users, carts, query strings), automatic purging on content changes, and a cron-based cache preloader so visitors never hit a cold page.
  • JavaScript — defer scripts and delay them until the first user interaction to cut Total Blocking Time, with an exclusion list.
  • CSS — minify, combine, and load CSS asynchronously to remove render-blocking stylesheets.
  • Image Optimization — lazy-load images and iframes, add missing dimensions to prevent layout shift, generate and serve WebP/AVIF, bulk-compress your existing library, convert opaque PNGs to JPEG, and replace YouTube embeds with a click-to-load preview.
  • Fonts — add font-display: swap, preconnect to font hosts, and preload font files.
  • Database — clean revisions, auto-drafts, trashed posts, spam/trashed comments and expired transients, optimize tables, and schedule automatic cleanups.
  • Heartbeat — reduce or disable the WordPress Heartbeat API per context to lower server load.
  • Tweaks — disable emojis, embeds, dashicons, query strings, XML-RPC and pingbacks, and add DNS-prefetch / preconnect hints.
  • CDN — rewrite static asset URLs to your CDN hostname.

A live performance score on the dashboard shows which optimizations are active and your biggest remaining win.

Build process and source code

The admin interface is a React application. The human-readable source lives in the src/ directory shipped inside the plugin (src/index.js and src/index.scss), and the compiled, minified output lives in build/.

To regenerate the compiled files from source:

  1. Install dependencies: npm install
  2. Build: npm run build

This uses the official @wordpress/scripts (webpack) toolchain — no custom or hidden build configuration. All source and build tooling are included in the plugin; nothing is obfuscated.

External services

Optimazz does not require any external service to function, and it works entirely on your own server by default. Two optional, admin-controlled features can reference third-party hosts:

  1. Google Fonts optimization (Fonts module). If — and only if — your theme or another plugin already loads Google Fonts, and you enable the Fonts module, Optimazz adds preconnect resource hints to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com and can add display=swap to the existing font URL. Optimazz does not add Google Fonts to a site that isn’t already using them, and it does not send any personal or site data — a preconnect is only a browser hint to open a connection earlier. The fonts themselves are requested by the visitor’s browser from Google, exactly as they were before the plugin, under Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms and privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

  2. CDN rewriting (CDN module). If you enable the CDN module and enter a CDN hostname, Optimazz rewrites the URLs of your own static assets (CSS, JS, images) to that hostname so visitors’ browsers load them from your CDN. The CDN is a service you choose and configure; Optimazz sends no data to it itself and is not affiliated with any CDN provider. Consult your chosen CDN’s own terms and privacy policy.

Both features are off by default and take effect only after you explicitly enable them.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the optimazz folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open Optimazz in the admin menu and enable the modules you want.
sections.faq:
Does Optimazz work alongside another caching plugin?

Optimazz will not overwrite another caching plugin’s advanced-cache.php drop-in. To use Optimazz page caching, deactivate any other page-caching plugin first. The other (non-caching) modules work alongside most plugins.

Will page caching work on my host?

Page caching needs WP_CACHE to be defined, which Optimazz adds to wp-config.php automatically. If wp-config.php is not writable, Optimazz shows a notice with the line to add manually.

Is it safe to delay JavaScript?

Delay-until-interaction is the biggest speed win but can affect scripts that must run before interaction. Start with “Delay” on and “Delay all” off, then add any problematic script keywords to the exclusion list.

Does converting PNG to JPEG lose my originals?

Only opaque PNGs are converted, the original is optionally backed up to uploads/optimazz-backup, and the conversion is rolled back if anything fails.

Does the plugin phone home or collect data?

No. Optimazz does not track users, register accounts, or send any of your site’s or visitors’ data to Optimazz servers. See the “External services” section for the only optional third-party hints the plugin can add.

Why does the plugin add inline <script> and <style> tags to my pages?

Those small inline fragments (the delay-JavaScript loader, critical/async CSS, the lazy-load helper and LCP preload hints) are the actual optimization output that Optimazz writes into your front-end HTML. They are the product of the plugin’s work, not the plugin’s own asset loading — a delay-until-interaction loader cannot be enqueued as an external file. The admin interface and all of the plugin’s own assets are loaded normally through the WordPress enqueue functions.
sections.changelog:
1.0.14

  • Fixed: enabling CSS optimization no longer makes a theme’s accessibility “skip links” (e.g. “Skip to content”) flash into the header on page load. Some themes hide these off-screen with a CSS transition; Optimazz now suppresses that transition on the common skip-link / screen-reader classes so they stay hidden (and still appear instantly on keyboard focus). Filterable via optimazz_skiplink_guard_css.
  • Fixed: bulk image compression / conversion no longer stops with a “critical error” on large libraries. A single image the host cannot process (usually a very large one that would exhaust memory) is now skipped cleanly, the job only stops after many consecutive failures instead of a handful spread across the run, and the maximum image size that is attempted now scales to the server’s memory limit so it is skipped before it can crash the request.
  • New: Font loading mode (Fonts module) — choose Optional, Swap or Block for font-display. Optional eliminates the layout shift caused when a web font swaps in over the fallback (a major source of a high CLS score); it is forced onto Google Fonts URLs even when the theme hard-coded display=swap.
  • Improved: images and iframes now reserve their space with aspect-ratio so they no longer push content down as they load. This attacks Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) directly and works even on themes that force height:auto. It is applied only when the dimensions are known and never overrides an explicit CSS height.
  • Fixed: the settings dropdowns (select controls) now render with the proper bordered box and a single arrow, matching the rest of the interface.

1.0.13

  • New: a “Server Requirements” panel on the Tools screen shows what your host supports — PHP and WordPress versions, the image library (GD/Imagick), WebP and AVIF support, memory limit, execution time and WP-Cron — with clear warnings that explain why a feature may be unavailable or slow (for example, why WebP/AVIF cannot be generated on a given server).
  • Fixed: WebP/AVIF conversion could stop with “There has been a critical error on this website” on a large image. AVIF encoding in particular can exhaust memory or the execution time limit — an unrecoverable fatal that cannot be caught. Very large images are now skipped before encoding (a configurable megapixel ceiling that applies on both the GD and Imagick engines and even on hosts that report no memory limit), and AVIF is processed in smaller batches, so the job completes instead of crashing.
  • Improved: bulk media jobs now survive a single failed batch. If one image makes a request time out, the job skips that item and continues to the end instead of stopping with “The response is not a valid JSON response”.

1.0.12

  • Fixed: the “Cached pages” counter on the Dashboard counted the internal empty index.html protection files as pages, so it showed the wrong number (and 0 KB pages). It now counts only real cached pages.
  • Improved: the cache preloader is now firewall-friendly. It paces its requests, identifies itself with a clear user-agent, and — most importantly — stops immediately if the server or a security plugin/firewall responds with 403, 429 or 503, instead of continuing to send requests. This prevents the warmer from tripping a rate-limiter or web-application firewall, and the admin shows a clear message if warming was blocked. A new optimazz_preload_delay_ms filter tunes the pause between requests.

1.0.11

  • Fixed: bulk image compression and WebP/AVIF conversion could stop with “There has been a critical error on this website” when the image library hit a single file it could not process (a corrupt image, or a PHP 8 error from GD/Imagick). Each image is now processed defensively — a problematic file is skipped and the batch continues to the end, and the progress panel reports how many were skipped. Oversized images are also checked for both the GD and Imagick engines to avoid running out of memory.
  • Improved: better cache preloading. Warming now follows the whole site like a sitemap — home, static front and posts pages, every public post type (pages, posts and custom types), then the busiest category and tag archives — most-important first, instead of only pages and posts, so more of the site is served warm from cache. The live progress now shows an estimated time remaining. New optimazz_preload_max filter caps how many URLs are warmed.

1.0.10

  • New: “Remove unused CSS” — opt-in options under File Optimization → CSS. “Remove block-editor CSS on the front end” dequeues WordPress block-library and global styles (a large saving on classic or page-builder sites that do not render Gutenberg blocks on the front end), “Load WooCommerce CSS only on shop pages” stops WooCommerce stylesheets loading on pages that do not need them (kept on cart, checkout, account, product and shop), and “Load Easy Digital Downloads CSS only on EDD pages” does the same for EDD (kept on checkout, purchase confirmation, purchase history and download archives). Both cut render-blocking CSS and improve First Contentful Paint, especially on mobile. They remove whole known-unused stylesheets and never guess at individual rules, so they are safe and reversible. Developers can scope any other plugin’s stylesheets with the new optimazz_plugin_css_scopes filter.
  • Improved: refreshed the admin sidebar with a cleaner, consistent icon set.
  • Fixed: the admin screen no longer flickers while scrolling (the fixed action bar was repainting a blurred backdrop on every scroll frame), and the plugin version now sits neatly below the menu instead of leaving an empty gap at the bottom.

1.0.9

  • Fixed: the admin app (the React dashboard) can now be translated. It previously stayed in English even when the WordPress menu translated, because the plugin was not telling WordPress where the JavaScript translations live. It now calls wp_set_script_translations, so translated strings load in the dashboard (delivered automatically for translations on WordPress.org).
  • Fixed: deferring JavaScript no longer causes “jQuery is not defined” or “wp is not defined” errors that broke some layouts. jQuery, jQuery Migrate and WordPress core scripts are now always kept immediate (never deferred), because inline scripts on the page expect them to already exist; every other script is still deferred, so the performance benefit is preserved.
  • Improved: the action buttons (Clear & Preload, Preload, Purge cache and others) now have clearer, more responsive feedback — hover lift, press animation, a subtle busy indicator, an icon spin on Purge, and visible keyboard focus.
  • New: “Take over caching”. When the Cache health check finds that another caching plugin’s advanced-cache.php is blocking Optimazz — so pages are not actually cached and the site can feel slower — a one-click button now makes Optimazz the caching drop-in and enables WP_CACHE, so caching finally engages. The conflicting plugin is named where possible, and when wp-config.php is not writable the exact WP_CACHE line to add is shown. If that plugin is still active afterwards (it could reclaim the cache), Optimazz now warns and offers a one-click button to deactivate it.

1.0.8

  • Fixed: the main hero image (the Largest Contentful Paint element) is no longer lazy-loaded. Previously the biggest above-the-fold image could be given loading="lazy" and deprioritised, which made LCP slower after activating the plugin — most noticeably on mobile. The hero image is now always loaded eagerly at high priority (and preloaded), while below-the-fold images still lazy-load as before. This is the most important fix for “my site got slower after installing.”
  • New: common third-party scripts — Google Tag Manager and Analytics, Facebook and TikTok pixels, Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, chat widgets and similar — are now delayed until the first interaction by default when JavaScript delay is on. They do not affect what the visitor sees, so delaying them cuts mobile Total Blocking Time and improves responsiveness (a major mobile win), while jQuery, your theme, page builders and payment scripts are always kept immediate.
  • New: a “Cache health” check on the Page Cache screen. One click tells you whether pages are actually being served from cache (HIT) or rebuilt on every request (MISS), and flags the usual reasons caching fails to engage — another caching plugin owns advanced-cache.php, the drop-in is missing, WP_CACHE is not enabled, or wp-config.php is not writable. If a site felt slower after enabling optimizations, this shows why.
  • New: the Dashboard now shows a clear notice when file or media optimizations are enabled but Page Cache is off, with a one-click button to turn caching on. Running optimizations without caching rebuilds every page on each request and can make a site feel slower — this points users to the fix.
  • Fixed: the translation template (languages/optimazz.pot) was empty. It is now generated with WP-CLI’s i18n make-pot and contains every translatable string from the plugin (PHP and the React admin), so the plugin can be fully translated.

1.0.7

  • New: the Page Cache screen now has a “Browser cache headers” control that adds Expires / Cache-Control rules (on Apache and LiteSpeed) so repeat visits load CSS, JavaScript, images and fonts straight from the browser cache, plus a “Cache lifetime” setting for how long cached pages are kept before they are refreshed.
  • Fixed: bulk WebP/AVIF conversion (and image compression) could stop partway with “The response is not a valid JSON response” on low-memory hosts — the batch ran out of memory converting large images and the request died. The batch size now adapts to the host’s PHP memory limit (one image at a time on 128 MB hosts), oversized images that would exhaust memory are skipped rather than crashing the job, and WordPress’s image memory limit is raised where the host allows it. Large image libraries now convert reliably in small, safe steps.
  • Fixed: “Clear & Preload” and “Preload” could stop partway with the error “The response is not a valid JSON response” on larger page-builder or WooCommerce sites. The preloader now warms one page per request, so each call stays well within the server’s time limit and the progress bar advances smoothly to the end.
  • Fixed: the LCP image preload no longer targets the site logo. It now picks a genuine above-the-fold hero image, preloads it responsively (matching the image’s own srcset/sizes so the correctly sized file is fetched instead of the full-size original), preloads only a single image, and skips the preload when the image is served as WebP/AVIF — avoiding a duplicate download. This resolves a possible speed regression seen on some sites after 1.0.5.

1.0.6

  • Fixed: enabling “Combine CSS” no longer breaks the layout of mega-menus and page-builder sections. Stylesheets are now merged only in contiguous, same-media groups and kept in their original position, so a later stylesheet can still override an earlier one (the cascade is preserved instead of being hoisted to the top).
  • Improved: the Database “Optimize now” action now shows the same progress panel as the other tools, with an animated bar while cleanup runs.

1.0.5

  • Improved: “Clear & Preload” and “Preload” now show live progress — the cached-page count climbs in small batches as pages warm, with a progress panel, and the job resumes if you reload the page.
  • Fixed: WooCommerce cart, checkout and account pages are now never cached and never have their CSS/JS optimized, regardless of page slug or language. This prevents broken checkouts on the default settings. Payment scripts (Stripe, PayPal, and others) are also never delayed.
  • Fixed: delaying JavaScript no longer postpones the visible page. jQuery, your theme and Elementor scripts are now always kept immediate (even with “Delay all” on), so First and Largest Contentful Paint are not slowed on JavaScript-rendered sites. The fallback timer was also shortened.
  • New: JavaScript minification for inline scripts. It strips comments and whitespace while keeping line breaks, so it is safe against automatic-semicolon-insertion issues; strings, template literals and regular expressions are preserved.
  • New: the LCP (largest contentful paint) image is now preloaded by default when the Media module is enabled, for a faster mobile load.
  • New: the above-the-fold hero background image (used by page builders such as Elementor) is now detected and preloaded, and is never lazy-loaded, improving LCP on builder-based sites.
  • New: a Critical CSS field. Paste your above-the-fold CSS and enable “Load CSS asynchronously” to remove render-blocking CSS without a flash of unstyled content.
  • Fixed: with asynchronous CSS enabled, critical CSS was only inlined when “Combine CSS” was also on. It is now inlined in all cases, so async CSS no longer causes a flash of unstyled content.
  • Improved: the asynchronous-CSS and “Delay all scripts” options are now clearly labelled and warn about their effects.
  • Improved: settings with a small set of choices (cleanup frequency, Heartbeat behaviour, eager-image count) now use clean one-click button groups instead of dropdowns.

1.0.4

  • Fixed: bulk image optimization could hit a fatal out-of-memory error on very large images, stopping the whole job. Oversized images are now skipped safely.
  • Fixed: a rare image-resize failure could trigger a fatal error on PHP 8. The resize now falls back gracefully.
  • New: JavaScript defer and delay now have separate exclusion lists, so a script can be excluded from one without losing the other. Added “Never defer”, “Never delay” and “Never optimize” fields, each with guidance and examples.
  • Fixed: the “Delay these scripts” list is now shown in the admin (it was previously not reachable in the interface).
  • Improved: cleaner, self-explanatory exclusion fields, and removed an empty “No items found” suggestion box that appeared on keyword inputs.
  • Improved: the admin footer no longer overlaps the plugin’s own footer on the Optimazz screen.

1.0.3

  • Fixed: generated CSS files returned 403 on Apache/LiteSpeed servers, leaving pages unstyled. The cache directory now denies only its private files and allows the generated assets.
  • Fixed: editing a post now also clears its category, tag, author and date archives, the blog page and the feed. Previously only the post and home page were cleared, so archives could serve outdated content indefinitely.
  • Fixed: a new comment no longer clears the entire site cache — only the page it was posted on. Comment edits, approvals and deletions clear that page too.
  • Fixed: stylesheets are rewritten in place instead of being moved, preserving the cascade order of interleaved inline styles.
  • Fixed: the CSS minifier no longer collapses a descendant combinator before a pseudo-class (“.card :is(h1,h2)” kept intact), and no longer strips comment-like text inside CSS strings.
  • Fixed: a failed CSS combine no longer drops the stylesheets from the page.
  • Fixed: changing an optimization setting now purges the page cache, so stale markup is not served.
  • Fixed: per-user cache keys are derived from the full session cookie, preventing a forged cookie from reaching another user’s cached page.
  • Fixed: Dashboard “File Optimization” now shows as on when either JavaScript or CSS is enabled.
  • Fixed: the page cache no longer stores wp-admin, login, cron or XML-RPC requests.
  • Added fail-safe guards so a PCRE limit on very large pages can never blank the output.

1.0.1

  • Subdirectory-install-safe URL-to-path mapping for CSS/media optimization.
  • Simplified the WP_CACHE handling in wp-config.php to a single WP_Filesystem edit.
  • Included the React admin source (src/) and documented the build steps.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: page cache + preloader, JavaScript defer/delay, CSS minify/combine/async, image optimization (lazy-load, dimensions, WebP/AVIF, bulk compression, PNG→JPEG, YouTube facade), fonts, database cleanup, heartbeat control, tweaks, and CDN — with a React admin dashboard.

upgrade_notice.1.0.12: The cache preloader is now firewall-friendly — it paces its requests and stops immediately if a firewall or security plugin returns 403/429/503, so warming can no longer trip a rate-limiter. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.11: Smarter cache preloading — warming now follows the whole site like a sitemap (custom post types and category/tag archives too, most-important first) with a live time-remaining estimate. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.10: Adds opt-in "Remove unused CSS" options (block-editor CSS on the front end, WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads CSS off their own pages) that cut render-blocking CSS and improve First Contentful Paint, plus a refreshed sidebar and a fix for admin scroll flicker. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.9: Adds a one-click "Take over caching" fix for when another caching plugin blocks Optimazz — installs the drop-in and enables WP_CACHE so pages are actually cached. Recommended if Cache health shows a conflict.
upgrade_notice.1.0.8: Important mobile speed fix: the hero (LCP) image is no longer lazy-loaded, so Largest Contentful Paint is faster after activation — the main cause of "my site got slower." Also delays third-party scripts (analytics, pixels, chat) to cut mobile blocking time, adds a one-click "Cache health" check, and warns when optimizing without Page Cache. Strongly recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.7: Fixes bulk WebP/AVIF conversion and preload failing with "not a valid JSON response" on low-memory hosts (conversion now adapts to the memory limit and processes one image at a time when needed), and makes LCP image preloading smarter — no more preloading the logo or an oversized image, which could slow some sites after 1.0.5. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Fixes a layout break when "Combine CSS" is enabled on page-builder sites (mega-menus and sections no longer lose their styling), and adds a progress panel to database optimization. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.5: Important fix: WooCommerce checkout is now safe on default settings (never cached or JS-delayed). Also: delaying JavaScript no longer slows First/Largest Contentful Paint on JavaScript-rendered sites. Also adds inline JS minification, a Critical CSS field, LCP preload, and cleaner settings.
upgrade_notice.1.0.4: Fixes two possible fatal errors during image optimization, adds separate defer/delay exclusion lists, and polishes the admin interface. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.3: Important fix for Apache and LiteSpeed servers, where optimized CSS could be blocked and leave pages unstyled. Also includes a cache-key security fix. Upgrading is recommended.

screenshots.caption: Dashboard — live performance score, cache statistics, quick actions, and per-module on/off switches.
Page Cache — serve static HTML instead of running PHP, with separate mobile caching.
File Optimization — defer and delay JavaScript, and minify, combine and async-load CSS.
Media — lazy-load images and iframes, add missing dimensions, and convert to WebP/AVIF.
Fonts — font-display swap, preconnect to font hosts, and preload font files.
Preload — warm the cache automatically so visitors never hit a cold page.
Advanced Rules — fine-tune caching with URL, cookie, and user-agent exclusions.
Database — clean revisions, drafts, spam, and transients, and optimize tables.
Heartbeat — reduce or disable the WordPress Heartbeat API to lower server load.
Tweaks — disable emojis, embeds, query strings, XML-RPC, and other front-end bloat.
CDN — rewrite static asset URLs to your CDN hostname.
Tools — import, export, and reset your configuration.
